title: Two-catalyst micelle chemoton: each micelle ends up holding one catalyst kind, same-kind clusters grow by division, and a higher-yield kind is outgrown (yield/replication trade-off)
summary: The micelle chemoton with two catalysts K1, K2 that share the precursor (winner-take-all K_i^2 autocatalysis) and differ only in amphiphile yield (r2 = 1.3 r1; twin r2 = r1), both seeded as white noise (K0=0.02, WORLD_P env). Every ignited micelle holds a single kind (kinds_*.png, red K1 / green K2). With low amphiphile decay (kap=0.0015) the micelles multiply into same-kind clusters until a lamellar phase takes over at t~450; with kap=0.003-0.005 the population settles into a static lattice of one-kind micelles with no visible conversions and no turnover. In both regimes the higher-yield kind ends with less catalyst than in its identical twin (K2 total 316 vs 409 at kap=0.003; 357 vs 441 at kap=0.005; 272 vs 454 at t=344, kap=0.0015), because amphiphile production spends the precursor that autocatalysis needs. One seed per arm; kinds are assigned by the initial noise, so this tests heredity, not selection. No claims.
